review_notes: I reviewed the whole file as supplied (lines 1–151). I did not open the related sources, because the file has no candidate for this rubric. It defines one concrete graph, `rigidSixGraph`, and an adjacency simp lemma. It then proves back-and-forth, orbit-rank and Scott-rank facts about that graph. It defines no function or construction whose homomorphism, continuity, equivalence or action structure is exposed only as loose lemmas. `rigidSixGraph` is already a `SimpleGraph`, which is the standard bundled object. `rigidSixGraph_iso_eq_refl` could be restated as a `Subsingleton` or `Unique` instance on automorphisms. That would restate a result rather than expose missing structure, and I found no existing consumer that would gain from it, so I did not report it. The private lemmas `bfEquiv_one_rigidSixGraph`, `exists_separating_move_rigidSixGraph`, `bfEquiv_two_rigidSixGraph_iff` and `two_mem_orbitStable_rigidSixGraph` are proof-internal facts about the graph. No standard bundle fits them. My remaining uncertainty is that I did not check whether `SimpleGraph.Iso` already has a `Subsingleton` instance elsewhere, which would only matter for the optional restatement above.
